stem: Which zone of a town has the highest land values?

options.rationale: Correct: it is the most accessible point and in highest demand.
Land at the edge is usually cheapest.
Land here is cheaper than in the CBD.
Plots are large but land per square metre is cheaper than the CBD.

explanation: Accessibility makes CBD land the most valuable.

stem: Which model shows a town as a series of rings around the CBD?

options.rationale: Correct: Burgess's model is made of rings.
Hoyt's model is made of wedges along routes.
This model has several centres.
The hierarchy ranks settlements, not zones.

explanation: Burgess (1925): concentric rings.

stem: Which feature is typical of the CBD?

options.content: Tall office blocks with few permanent residents
options.rationale: Correct: offices and shops dominate and few people live there.

options.content: Large houses on big plots with gardens
options.rationale: This describes low-density residential areas.
These are found on the rural-urban fringe.
This describes the industrial zone.

explanation: The CBD has high-rise commercial buildings and few residents.

stem: Why are industrial zones often located beside railway lines?

options.content: Land beside railways is the most expensive in town
options.rationale: Industrial land is usually cheaper than CBD land.

options.content: Raw materials and products can be moved in bulk
options.rationale: Correct: rail access cuts transport costs for heavy goods.
Wealthy residents tend to avoid railways and industry.
Railways add noise rather than reducing it.

explanation: Industry needs transport for bulky inputs and outputs.

stem: In the sector model, where is low-income housing usually found?

options.rationale: That is the high-income zone of the concentric model.
The CBD is commercial, with few homes.
Correct: workers live near factories, on cheaper land.

options.content: Along the most attractive high ground
options.rationale: High ground usually attracts high-income housing.

explanation: Hoyt placed low-income housing next to the industrial sector.

stem: Which Harare suburb is a high-density residential area?

options.rationale: Borrowdale is a low-density northern suburb.
Correct: Mbare is Harare's oldest high-density suburb.
Mount Pleasant is a low-density northern suburb.
Msasa is mainly an industrial area.

explanation: High-density suburbs lie mainly to the south and west of Harare's CBD.

stem: A town has industry and high-density housing extending south-west along a railway, and low-density housing extending north-east. Which model does this pattern fit best?

options.rationale: That model has rings, not wedges in different directions.
Correct: wedges of land use extend outwards along routes.
The description has no separate centres.
That describes settlement hierarchy, not internal zones.

explanation: Opposite wedges of land use along routes are the sector model's key feature.
hints: Which model has wedges, and which has several centres?

stem: Which is the best reason why the Burgess model fits Harare poorly?

options.content: Harare has no central business district
options.rationale: Harare has a clear CBD.
Harare has several industrial areas.

options.content: Colonial planning placed residential areas by race in sectors
options.rationale: Correct: segregation, not rings of wealth, shaped the city.

options.content: Land values in Harare are lowest in the CBD and rise towards the edge
options.rationale: Land values are highest in the CBD.

explanation: Planning history produced sectors rather than concentric rings.
hints: Think about how Zimbabwean towns were planned before 1980.

stem: A study area contains smallholdings, a new shopping mall, a cemetery and a sewage works. Which zone is it most likely to be?

options.rationale: The CBD has no smallholdings or sewage works.
This zone has old factories and housing close to the CBD.
This zone is mainly houses.
Correct: a mix of farming and land-hungry urban uses on cheap land.

explanation: The fringe has cheap land and a mixture of rural and urban uses.
hints: What mixes urban and rural uses?

stem: The multiple-nuclei model shows a town growing round several centres rather than one.
explanation: True. Harris and Ullman's model has several nuclei.

stem: In the concentric zone model, the wealthiest people live in the zone of transition next to the CBD.
explanation: False. The zone of transition has deteriorating housing; the wealthiest live in the outer commuter zone.

stem: Match each zone with a typical land use or feature.

right.content: Large plots with gardens and trees
Smallholdings mixed with new housing estates
Factories and warehouses with railway sidings

explanation: Each zone has a characteristic land use.

stem: Choose the correct name for each model.

payload.template: The concentric zone model was proposed by {{blank:a}}, and the sector model by {{blank:b}}.

explanation: Burgess (1925) concentric; Hoyt (1939) sector; Harris and Ullman (1945) multiple nuclei.

stem: A fictional high-density housing scheme has 240 houses on 8 hectares. Calculate its residential density in houses per hectare.
explanation: 240 ÷ 8 = 30 houses per hectare.

stem: Pedestrian counts (fictional data) taken for 10 minutes at five sites along a road leading out of a CBD were 186, 142, 95, 61 and 26. Calculate the mean count.
explanation: 510 ÷ 5 = 102 pedestrians per 10 minutes.
hints: Add the counts and divide by the number of sites.

stem: Describe **four** characteristics of the central business district of a town.

points.description: Tall, high-rise buildings.
Offices, banks, large shops, hotels and government buildings.
Highest land values / rents.
Few residents; heavy traffic, congestion and many pedestrians by day.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The CBD has tall buildings housing offices, banks and large shops. Land values are the highest in the town. Few people live there, but it is crowded with traffic and pedestrians during the day.

explanation: Give features that could be observed.

stem: Explain why high-density suburbs in Harare are mostly located close to industrial areas.

points.description: Workers can walk or use cheap transport to factories.
Land near industry is cheaper / less attractive, so suited to low-cost housing.
Colonial planning placed townships for African workers near industry and away from low-density suburbs.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Workers can reach the factories cheaply on foot or by kombi. Land near industry is cheaper and less pleasant, so it was used for low-cost housing, and colonial planners deliberately placed workers' townships there, away from the low-density suburbs.

explanation: Link each reason to the location.
hints: Think about cost of land, journey to work and planning history.

stem: With reference to Harare or Bulawayo, evaluate how well the concentric zone, sector and multiple-nuclei models describe the town's land use.

points.description: Names the town and describes its CBD.
Describes industrial areas (e.g. Workington, Southerton, Msasa in Harare) and their position near railways.
Describes high-density suburbs (e.g. Mbare, Highfield, Glen View) mainly to the south and west.
Describes low-density suburbs (e.g. Borrowdale, Mount Pleasant) mainly to the north and north-east.
Sector model fits: wedges of industry with high-density housing, low-density housing in the opposite direction.
Multiple-nuclei fits: suburban shopping and office centres, satellite towns; concentric fits poorly.
Judgement with reasons: colonial planning, relief, informal growth explain the departures from the models.

levels.descriptor: Developed, accurate explanation of several relevant points, supported by a located example or the resource, with a clear judgement or conclusion where the question asks for one.
Some explanation of relevant points, partly developed; an example or resource evidence is used in general terms; any judgement is simple or one-sided.
Simple statements or a list of points with little explanation; no example or only a name.

answerSpec.modelAnswer: Harare has a clear CBD of high-rise offices, banks and shops with the highest land values, which matches all three models. Industry lies mainly south and south-west along the railway in areas such as Workington and Southerton, with more in Msasa to the east. High-density suburbs such as Mbare, Highfield and Glen View lie mainly to the south and west near industry, while low-density suburbs such as Borrowdale and Mount Pleasant lie to the north and north-east. These wedges of land use match Hoyt's sector model well. Suburban shopping and office centres in the northern suburbs, and satellite towns such as Chitungwiza, show multiple nuclei. The concentric model fits poorly because wealth does not increase in rings outwards; instead colonial planning separated residential areas by race into sectors. Overall Harare is best described as a sector model with multiple nuclei, but no model fits perfectly because of its planning history, relief and recent informal growth at the edges.

explanation: Describe the real town, compare with each model and judge.
hints: Describe Harare's zones, then compare each model.
End with which model fits best and why.

stem:
Table 1 shows land use along a transect from the centre of a fictional town (fictional data).

| Distance from centre (km) | Main land use | Typical building height (storeys) | Plot size (m²) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 | Offices and shops | 12 | 400 |
| 1.5 | Factories and warehouses | 2 | 5,000 |
| 3.0 | Houses | 1 | 300 |
| 6.0 | Houses | 1 | 2,000 |
| 9.0 | Smallholdings and a new mall | 1 | 20,000 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which zone is found at 3.0 km?

options.rationale: Low-density plots are large, like the 2,000 m² at 6 km.
The CBD is at 0.5 km with tall buildings.
The fringe is at 9 km.
Correct: small plots of 300 m² with single-storey houses.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: How many times larger is a plot at 6.0 km than a plot at 3.0 km? Give your answer to one decimal place.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Describe how building height changes with distance from the centre.

points.description: Building height is greatest at the centre (12 storeys at 0.5 km).
It falls sharply away from the centre to 1-2 storeys beyond 1.5 km.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Buildings are tallest in the centre (12 storeys) and fall to 2 storeys at 1.5 km and 1 storey further out.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain why buildings are tallest near the centre.

points.description: The centre is the most accessible place, so demand for land is highest.
Land values/rents are therefore highest.
Building upwards makes the most of expensive land / businesses there can afford high rents.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The centre is where routes meet, so it is the most accessible place and many businesses want to locate there. This makes land very expensive, so developers build upwards to fit more floor space on each plot.

explanation: This item practises interpreting a land-use transect.
hints: Use building height and plot size together.

stem: A description of a fictional town: the CBD lies at a road and rail junction. A railway runs from the CBD to the south-west, with factories along it and small council houses on either side. A main road runs north-east to a reservoir, with large houses on hills along it. A university with its own shops lies 6 km east of the CBD.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: The factories and council houses along the railway best match which feature of the sector model?

options.content: A concentric ring of high-income commuter housing
options.rationale: Rings are part of the concentric model.
That is part of the multiple-nuclei model.
That is a ring round the CBD in the concentric model.

options.content: An industrial sector with low-income housing beside it
options.rationale: Correct: a wedge along a transport route.

parts.explanation: Hoyt's industrial sector follows a transport route.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Suggest **two** reasons why large houses have been built on the hills along the road to the north-east.

points.description: Away from factory noise and pollution / on the opposite side of town to industry.
Pleasant views, cooler, well-drained hills / near the reservoir; residents have cars to travel along the main road.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The hills are far from the factories in the south-west, so they are quieter and cleaner, and they have attractive views over the reservoir.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Which feature of the town suggests the multiple-nuclei model? Explain your answer.

points.description: The university with its own shops 6 km east of the CBD.
It forms a separate centre (nucleus) of activity away from the CBD.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The university with its own shops is a second centre of activity, separate from the CBD, which is what the multiple-nuclei model shows.

parts.explanation: A nucleus is a separate centre.

explanation: This item practises applying urban models to a described town.
hints: Look for wedges and separate centres.
